decisions.title: Use Dafny for core logic
decisions.context: Core scheduling logic is complex and error-prone
decisions.decision: Implement all core logic in Dafny with verified contracts
decisions.consequences: Higher upfront cost but fewer runtime bugs

decisions.title: Use relational database for job store
decisions.context: Need ACID transactions for job state
decisions.decision: Use a relational database for job and dead letter storage
decisions.consequences: Simpler consistency model, but less flexible than NoSQL

openRisks.mitigation: Heartbeat monitoring and job re-dispatch with idempotency keys

components.name: SchedulerCore
components.internals: Uses pipeline pattern for parse-validate-transform-store of job definitions; uses graph pattern for DAG traversal; uses scheduler pattern for ready-job selection. No I/O; all external effects via extern portals.

testCases.name: ParseValidCronExpression
testCases.description: Parse a valid cron expression '0 0 * * *'
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a CronExpression with minute=0, hour=0, dayOfMonth=*, month=*, dayOfWeek=*

testCases.name: RejectInvalidCronExpression
testCases.description: Parse an invalid cron expression '61 0 * * *'
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns failure with error message

testCases.name: BuildDagFromDependencies
testCases.description: Build a DAG from job definitions with dependencies
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a JobDag with correct nodes and edges

testCases.name: DetectCycleInDag
testCases.description: Build a DAG with a cycle
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns failure with cycle detected

testCases.name: SelectReadyJobs
testCases.description: Given a DAG and completed jobs, select jobs whose dependencies are satisfied
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns the set of ready jobs

components.responsibility: Core scheduling engine: parses cron expressions, validates job definitions, builds and traverses the job dependency DAG, determines ready jobs, and emits execution requests.

components.name: JobStore
components.internals: Uses repository pattern for entity storage. Pure Dafny logic with extern portals for database I/O.

testCases.name: SaveAndRetrieveJob
testCases.description: Save a job record and retrieve it by ID
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns the same job record

testCases.name: UpdateJobStatus
testCases.description: Update the status of an existing job
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns the updated job with new status

testCases.name: QueryJobsByStatus
testCases.description: Query jobs by status
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns only jobs with the given status

components.responsibility: Persistent storage and retrieval of job definitions, job instances, and job status. Provides CRUD operations and status queries.

components.name: WorkerPool
components.internals: Uses state-machine pattern for worker lifecycle (idle, busy, failed). Pure Dafny logic with extern portals for network I/O.

testCases.name: AssignJobToAvailableWorker
testCases.description: Assign a job to an available worker
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a WorkerAssignment with the worker marked busy

testCases.name: RejectWhenNoWorkers
testCases.description: Attempt to assign a job when no workers are available
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns failure with no workers available

testCases.name: MarkWorkerFailed
testCases.description: Mark a worker as failed
testCases.expectedBehavior: Worker status becomes failed and is removed from available pool

components.responsibility: Manages a pool of worker nodes, assigns execution requests to available workers, tracks worker health, and handles worker failure.

components.name: RetryManager
components.internals: Uses state-machine pattern for retry lifecycle. Pure Dafny logic with extern portals for time.

testCases.name: ComputeBackoffDelay
testCases.description: Compute backoff delay for retry attempt 3 with base delay 1 second
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns 4 seconds (2^3 * 1)

testCases.name: ExceedMaxRetries
testCases.description: Check if retry count exceeds max retries
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns true and indicates dead letter

testCases.name: ScheduleNextRetry
testCases.description: Schedule next retry time based on backoff
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a time in the future

components.responsibility: Implements retry logic with exponential backoff. Tracks retry counts, computes next retry time, and decides when to give up and route to dead letter queue.

components.name: DeadLetterQueue
components.internals: Uses repository pattern for storage. Pure Dafny logic with extern portals for database I/O.

testCases.name: EnqueueDeadLetter
testCases.description: Enqueue a dead letter record
testCases.expectedBehavior: Record is stored and can be retrieved

testCases.name: DequeueDeadLetter
testCases.description: Dequeue a dead letter record
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns the record and removes it from the queue

testCases.name: InspectQueue
testCases.description: Inspect the queue contents
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns all dead letter records

components.responsibility: Stores jobs that have permanently failed after exhausting retries. Provides enqueue, dequeue, and inspection operations.

components.name: StatusTracker
components.internals: Uses reducer pattern for state transitions. Pure Dafny logic with extern portals for database I/O.

testCases.name: RecordStatusTransition
testCases.description: Record a status transition from scheduled to running
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a new status event and updates the job status

testCases.name: RejectInvalidTransition
testCases.description: Attempt to transition from succeeded to running
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns failure with invalid transition

testCases.name: GetJobHistory
testCases.description: Get the status history for a job
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns all status events for the job in order

components.responsibility: Tracks and reports job status transitions (scheduled, running, succeeded, failed, dead-lettered). Maintains a history of status changes.

components.name: SchedulerApi
components.internals: ASP.NET Core Web API. Thin I/O shell that translates HTTP requests to SchedulerCore calls.

testCases.name: SubmitJobEndpoint
testCases.description: POST /jobs with a valid job definition
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns 201 Created with job ID

testCases.name: GetJobStatusEndpoint
testCases.description: GET /jobs/{id}/status
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns 200 OK with current status

testCases.name: ListDeadLettersEndpoint
testCases.description: GET /dead-letters
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns 200 OK with list of dead letter records

components.responsibility: HTTP API for submitting jobs, querying status, and managing the scheduler. Exposes REST endpoints.

components.name: SchedulerCli
components.internals: Console application. Thin I/O shell that parses commands and calls SchedulerCore.

testCases.name: SubmitJobCommand
testCases.description: Run 'submit --cron "0 0 * * *" --command "echo hello"'
testCases.expectedBehavior: Prints job ID and exits with code 0

testCases.name: StatusCommand
testCases.description: Run 'status --job-id 123'
testCases.expectedBehavior: Prints current status and exits with code 0

testCases.name: InvalidCommand
testCases.description: Run an unknown command
testCases.expectedBehavior: Prints error and exits with non-zero code

components.responsibility: Command-line interface for interacting with the scheduler: submit jobs, view status, manage workers.

dataStores.name: JobDatabase
dataStores.schema: jobs(id, definition, status, retry_count, next_retry_time, created_at, updated_at); job_dependencies(job_id, dependency_id); status_history(job_id, status, timestamp)

systemContext: A distributed task scheduler that accepts cron expressions and DAG-based job dependencies, manages a worker pool, retries failed jobs with exponential backoff, routes permanently failed jobs to a dead letter queue, and tracks job status throughout the lifecycle.

qualityAttributes.rationale: Distributed scheduler must be highly available

deploymentTopology: Scheduler core and API deployed as a single service. Worker pool runs as separate processes on multiple nodes. Database is a shared relational store. Dead letter queue is part of the same database.
